result.topic_en: Euler derives series expressions in the eccentric anomaly V for the Sun's distance, apparent diameter and semidiameter, horizontal parallax, and hourly motion, with numerical values at apogee and perigee.
result.transcription:
384 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA.
Porro si ponatur $y$ distantia solis a terra, et $a$ distantia media, erit
$y = a(1 + e\cos V)$,
pro $a$ vero in tabulis usurpari solet numerus 100000. Quando autem sol in hac distantia media [?] a terra versatur, ejus diameter apparens deprehenditur $32'13''$. In distantia ergo $y = a(1 + e\cos V)$ [?]
erit diameter solis apparens
$= \frac{32'13''}{1 + e\cos V} = \frac{1933''}{1 + e\cos V}$:
Evoluto autem hoc denominatore prodibit diameter apparens
$= 1933''(1 - e\cos V + \tfrac{1}{2}ee + \tfrac{1}{2}ee\cos 2V - \tfrac{3}{4}e^3\cos V - \tfrac{1}{4}e^3\cos 3V)$;
et si parallaxis horizontalis in distantia media statuatur $= 12\tfrac{1}{2}''$, erit pro quavis distantia $y$, quae [?]
anomaliae excentricae $V$ convenit, parallaxis horizontalis solis
$= 12,5\,(1 + \tfrac{1}{2}ee - (e + \tfrac{3}{4}e^3)\cos V + \tfrac{1}{2}ee\cos 2V - \tfrac{1}{4}e^3\cos 3V)$.
§ 2. Posito autem pro $e$ valore supra invento erit
$1 + \tfrac{1}{2}ee = 1,0001405$, $\quad e + \tfrac{3}{4}e^3 = 0,0167630$
$\tfrac{1}{2}ee = 0,0001405$, $\quad \tfrac{1}{4}e^3 = 0,0000012$.
Hinc anomaliae excentricae $V$ respondebit diameter solis apparens in minutis secundis
$1933'' - 32,4\cos V \quad + 0,27\cos 2V$
$(1,5105718) \quad (9,4323278)$
cum ergo terminus ultimus ne dimidium quidem minutum secundum praebeat, erit
diameter solis apparens $= 32'13'' - 32,4\cos V$
$(1,5105718)$
semidiam. solis apparens $= 16\;\; 6\tfrac{1}{2} - 16,2\cos V$
$(1,2095418)$
Parallaxis autem solis horizontalis anomaliae excentricae $V$ respondens erit $= 12\tfrac{1}{2}'' - 0,2\cos V$.
In apogeo ergo parallaxis solis fere erit $12''$, in perigeo vero $13''$, unde hoc calculo fere supersedere poterimus.
§ 3. Quod ad motum solis horarium attinet, eum ex aequatione differentiali $d\theta = \frac{dV\sqrt{(1-ee)}}{1 + e\cos V}$
definiri conveniet. Cum enim sit $dV = \frac{dU}{1 + e\cos V}$, erit $d\theta = \frac{\sqrt{(1-ee)}}{(1 + e\cos V)^2}dU$, unde si $dU$ denotet
motum horarium anomaliae solis mediae, qui est $= 2'27\tfrac{5}{6}''$, valor ipsius $d\theta$ erit motus horarius
verus solis. Hinc ergo pro anomalia excentrica $V$ erit motus horarius solis
$= 147'',833\,(1 + ee - (2e + 2e^3)\cos V + \tfrac{3}{2}ee\cos 2V - e^3\cos 3V)$
$= 147'',833\,(1,0002809 - 0,0335284\cos V + 0,0004214\cos 2V)$.
His ergo factoribus evolutis erit
motus horarius solis $= 147'',87 - 4,9566\cos V$.
$(0,6951839)$
In apogeo ergo est motus horarius solis $= 142'',92 = 2'23''$
in perigeo vero erit motus horarius solis $= 152'',86 = 2\;33$.

items.quote: In apogeo ergo parallaxis solis fere erit $12''$, in perigeo vero $13''$, unde hoc calculo fere supersedere poterimus.
items.english: Therefore at apogee the solar parallax will be about 12'', at perigee 13'', so we can nearly dispense with this calculation.
The hourly motion of the Sun = 147.87'' - 4.9566 cos V.
